area: Health and budget rules (findExceptions health/budget loops, budgetStatus, tiles() 'Spend vs budget', budget() chart/table/tooltip, rules() budget rows)
summary: On the committed data the health and budget rules give the right answers. I summed every month by hand and got the same results: Booster 15 days overdue (serious), Pinkeye due in 3 days (warning), Fuel 21% over ($2,040) and Repairs 25% over ($1,800), both serious, and a tile of +1.0% with $89,303 of $88,400. Health results are the same in every time zone I tried. The weak point is input that differs from the generator's exact format. Three problems rate high. (1) A health status of 'Open', 'OPEN', 'open ' (trailing space), 'in progress' or 'scheduled' makes an overdue vaccination disappear without any message. Health data appears nowhere else on the page, so nothing shows it. (2) budgetStatus ignores the month column. If the season plan is loaded up front (Oct/Nov rows with actual 0), both overspend alerts disappear and the tile reads −32.7%. Missing or blank months go unnoticed. (3) A blank or '(300)' amount turns the totals into text through `+=`. The Fuel alert disappears, and the headline tile shows things like '−89.8% $89,803 of $884,000', '+2.715256118778953e+22%' or '−NaN% $NaN'. Medium: a zero-budget category prints 'Infinity% over'. A zero budget or an unreadable amount turns every bar coordinate into NaN, so the budget chart draws no bars. Also medium: an open task with no due date is never shown. The committed 'Fly tag check' row (done, due Sep 1, last done Jun 5) contradicts itself and isn't flagged. Thresholds are percent only ($30 over on $200 is serious; $9,500 over on $100,000 is a warning). Within a severity, rows are sorted A–Z by area, so Budget rows come before an overdue vaccine and a silent water sensor. Low: exactly 5% gets no alert even though the rules say '5-10%'; 9.6% and 10.4% both print '10% over' at different severities; amounts with cents can tip an exact 10.00% into serious; '$104.5' dollar formatting; 'Due in 0 days'; '−0.0%', '−0%' and 'Under by $0' when exactly on budget; overlapping chart labels at −40%; '7.000000000000001-10%' after tuning a threshold. One suspicion turned out wrong: whole-dollar 1,100 vs 1,000 gives pct exactly 0.1, because the code computes (a−b)/b. Overlap with other auditors: CSV-56/57 (csv.repro), TIME-14/15/18/D1 (time.repro), TB-06 (time.browser), B-07 (csv.browser). Repro script: 9 MATCH (controls), 35 MISMATCH, 0 threw.
trace:
HEALTH. data/health.csv (group,task,last_done,next_due,status) -> parseCSV: dates stay strings because +"2026-09-15" is NaN, and a blank cell becomes "". findExceptions (exceptions.js:140-147) skips a row unless `h.status === "open"` exactly and next_due is truthy. It then computes left = days(asOf.slice(0,10), h.next_due) = (new Date(next_due) - new Date("2026-09-30"))/864e5. Both are date-only strings, read as UTC midnight, so left is a whole number of days in any zone (case HB-C8). left < 0 -> serious, subject "<group>: <task>", problem "Overdue by N day(s) (due D)", action "Schedule it this week". 0 <= left <= 7 -> warning "Due in N day(s) (D)", action "Plan it with the next gather". left > 7 or NaN -> nothing. last_done is never read. Results are sorted by SEVERITY, then area A-Z (line 158). In app.js the rows feed exceptionsTable (innerHTML), the Health chip count and the 'Needs attention' tile. Health data is shown nowhere else on the page. Committed data: Booster due Sep 15 -> 15 days overdue, serious. Pinkeye due Oct 3 -> 3 days, warning. Pregnancy check (Oct 25, 25 days) and Deworm (Nov 1, 32 days) -> no row. The two 'done' rows are skipped, including Fly tag check with next_due Sep 1.
BUDGET. data/budget.csv (month,category,budget,actual) -> parseCSV: numbers become Number; a blank cell or '(300)' stays a string. budgetStatus (exceptions.js:82-89) groups by category only; month and as_of are ignored. It runs `c.budget += r.budget; c.actual += r.actual`, then variance = actual - budget and pct = variance / budget. findExceptions (149-156) builds text = Math.round(pct*100)+'% over'. pct > 0.10 -> serious "N% over season to date ($variance.toLocaleString())", action "Find what drove it and decide whether to re-forecast". pct > 0.05 -> warning "N% over season to date", action "Watch it next month". In app.js: tiles() (49, 57) sets tb = sum of budgets and ta = sum of actuals; the value is (ta > tb ? '+' : '−') + |ta-tb|/tb*100 to 1 decimal; the detail is money(ta) 'of' money(tb) ', season to date'. budget() (178-198) sorts rows by pct descending, sets lim = max(0.3, |pct|...) and x(v) = m.l + (v+lim)/(2lim)*width. Bars run from x(0) to x(pct), red when pct > 0. Labels are ± round(|pct|*100)%. The tooltip shows Budget/Actual/'Over|Under by'; the table shows money() values with '+' only when variance > 0. rules() (213-214) prints R.budgetSerious*100 and R.budgetWarn*100. Committed data: Fuel 2592+2928+3120+3000 = 11,640 vs 9,600 -> +2,040 = 21.25% -> serious '21% over season to date ($2,040)'. Repairs 9,000 vs 7,200 -> +1,800 = 25% -> serious. Feed −3.2%, Vet −0.9%, Labor −4.8%, Water −7.1% -> no row. Tile: 89,303 vs 88,400 = +1.02% -> '+1.0%'. Chart labels in order: Repairs +25%, Fuel +21%, Vet −1%, Feed −3%, Labor −5%, Water and fencing −7%. All of these were observed (HB-C2, AB-00).

findings.title: Health status must be exactly 'open'; 'Open', 'OPEN', 'open ', 'in progress', 'scheduled' and 'overdue' silently drop an overdue vaccination
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/healthbudget.repro.mjs, cases H-01a/b/c and H-02a/b/c. Minimal input: health.csv row 'Yearlings,Booster vaccine,2026-06-02,2026-09-15,Open' (for 'open ' it is followed by another row, because parseCSV trims the end of the file), as_of 2026-09-30T18:00.
findings.expected: serious | Yearlings: Booster vaccine | Overdue by 15 days (due 2026-09-15) (calendar: Sep 15 -> Sep 30 = 15 days). For a status the rule doesn't know, at least a row saying the status was not recognised.
findings.actual: H-01a 'Open': "(no alerts)". H-01b 'OPEN': "(no alerts)". H-01c 'open ': "(no alerts)". H-02a 'in progress', H-02b 'scheduled', H-02c 'overdue': "(no alerts)" in each case.
findings.consequence: Missed alert. A booster 15 days overdue vanishes from the report, the Health chip count and the 'Needs attention' tile, just because someone typed 'Open' in a spreadsheet or marked the task 'in progress'. Health data has no other view on the page, so the manager gets a false all-clear on herd health.
findings.regression_test: In tests/exceptions.test.mjs, build health rows inline with as_of 2026-09-30T18:00. For s of ['Open','OPEN','open ']: rows `Yearlings,Booster vaccine,2026-06-02,2026-09-15,${s}` plus `Yearlings,Deworm,2026-06-02,2026-11-01,open`. Assert the Health alerts deep-equal [['serious','Overdue by 15 days (due 2026-09-15)']]. The 15 is counted on the calendar: Sep 15 to Sep 30. For s of ['in progress','scheduled']: assert some Health alert has subject 'Yearlings: Booster vaccine'. For 'cancelled' and 'done': assert no alert (this already passes; case HB-C5).
findings.proposed_fix: Normalise first: const st = String(h.status ?? '').trim().toLowerCase(). Treat a small closed set ('done', 'complete', 'completed', 'cancelled', 'canceled') as closed. Judge every other status as open. When the status is not 'open', add a warning row "Status '<raw>' not recognised; treated as open". List the accepted values in the README.

findings.title: budgetStatus ignores the month column: future plan rows, a blank current month, or a missing month change 'season to date' and can hide overspend
findings.location: exceptions.js:82-89 (month and as_of never read), exceptions.js:149-156, app.js:49,57
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/healthbudget.repro.mjs, cases BU-06/AB-07 (committed data plus rows '2026-10,<cat>,<plan>,0' and '2026-11,<cat>,<plan>,0' for all 6 categories), BU-04/AB-08 (Sep Fuel actual blank), and BU-07 (Sep Fuel row deleted).
findings.expected: With as_of 2026-09-30, season to date is Jun-Sep. Fuel stays serious at 21% ($2,040) and Repairs at 25% ($1,800). The tile stays '+1.0%  $89,303 of $88,400'. If Sep Fuel is blank: Fuel is serious at 20% on Jun-Aug (8,640 vs 7,200), or there is a 'September Fuel actual missing' row. If the Sep Fuel row is deleted: a row noting the missing month.
findings.actual: BU-06: "Fuel 11640/14400 = -19.2%; Repairs 9000/10800 = -16.7%; (no alerts)". AB-07 tile: "SPEND VS BUDGET −32.7% $89,303 of $132,600, season to date", budget report rows "". BU-04: "Fuel actual=\"8640\" (string) pct=-0.1; serious | Repairs | 25% over ...", so the Fuel alert is gone, and the chart label shows Fuel "−10%". BU-07: "serious | Fuel | 20% over season to date ($1,440)", still called 'season to date', with no mention that September is missing.
findings.consequence: Missed alert and a misleading all-clear. Loading the season's budget up front, which is the normal way to load a budget, makes both real overspends disappear, and the headline tile says spending is 32.7% under budget. Bookkeeping that lags a month does the same for that category. The manager decides not to re-forecast on false numbers.
findings.regression_test: Append Oct and Nov rows (budget = monthly plan, actual 0) for all six categories to the committed budget.csv. Assert the Budget alerts deep-equal [['serious','Fuel','21% over season to date ($2,040)'], ['serious','Repairs','25% over season to date ($1,800)']]. Hand sums: Fuel 2592+2928+3120+3000 = 11,640 vs 4×2400 = 9,600; Repairs 1620+2520+1980+2880 = 9,000 vs 4×1800 = 7,200. Browser: the tile contains '+1.0%' and '$89,303 of $88,400'. Then set the 2026-09 Fuel actual to blank. Assert there is either a Fuel serious row with '20% over' (Jun-Aug: 8,640 vs 7,200) or a warning naming 2026-09 and Fuel.
findings.proposed_fix: Pass asOf into budgetStatus. Include only rows with month <= asOf.slice(0,7). For the as_of month, either exclude it until it is closed (and say 'through August') or prorate its budget by days elapsed. Treat a blank actual as 'not entered', not 0. Exclude that month's budget for the category and add a warning 'Fuel: 2026-09 actual not entered'. Check that every category has a row for every month in range and report any gaps. Change the tile detail to name the months covered.

findings.title: Blank or accounting-format amounts ('', '(300)') turn budget totals into strings via +=: Fuel/Repairs alerts vanish and the headline tile shows $884,000, e+22% or NaN
findings.location: exceptions.js:30 (non-numeric cells stay strings), exceptions.js:86 (c.budget += r.budget; c.actual += r.actual), app.js:49 (tile reduce), app.js:57
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/healthbudget.repro.mjs, cases BU-03/AB-03 (committed data + '2026-09,Hay,,500'), AB-08 (Sep Fuel actual blank: '2026-09,Fuel,2400,') and BU-05/AB-10 (committed data + '2026-09,Repairs,0,(300)').
findings.expected: AB-03 tile: '+1.6%  $89,803 of $88,400' (budget unchanged at 88,400; actual 89,303 + 500 = 89,803; 1,403/88,400 = 1.59%). BU-05: Repairs serious, 8,700 vs 7,200 = 20.8% over ($1,500), or an 'unreadable amount' row. AB-08: a small finite percentage (about +0.4% with Sep Fuel left out of both sides: 86,303 vs 86,000).
findings.actual: BU-03: "budget=\"0\" (string)". AB-03 tile: "SPEND VS BUDGET −89.8% $89,803 of $884,000, season to date". AB-08 tile: "SPEND VS BUDGET +2.715256118778953e+22% $24,002,864,090,005,946,000,000,000 of $88,400, season to date", and the report keeps only Repairs. BU-05: "Repairs actual=\"9000(300)\" pct=NaN", so the Repairs alert is gone. AB-10 tile: "SPEND VS BUDGET −NaN% $NaN of $88,400", Repairs bar label "−NaN%", 18 NaN attributes in the chart.
findings.consequence: One blank cell or one refund typed the accountant's way (in parentheses) erases a real serious overspend alert. The top-of-page tile then shows a nonsense number, or worse a believable one: '−89.8%' reads as 'well under budget'. A hiring manager who loads their own export would see this right away.
findings.regression_test: budgetStatus(parseCSV(committed + '\n2026-09,Hay,,500')) -> every budget and actual has typeof 'number'. Hay has budget 0 and actual 500. The Budget totals are 88,400 and 89,803, summed by hand from the CSV. findExceptions(committed + '2026-09,Repairs,0,(300)') -> a Repairs serious row containing '21% over' and '$1,500' (9,000 − 300 = 8,700; 8,700 − 7,200 = 1,500; 1,500/7,200 = 20.8%). Browser AB-03: the tile contains '+1.6%' and '$89,803 of $88,400'.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a strict money parser for budget amounts. '' means missing, counted separately and never added. '(300)' becomes −300. '$3,000' becomes 3000. Any other value raises a data-quality row ('Repairs 2026-09 actual "x" can't be read'). budgetStatus should only ever add Numbers (Number.isFinite guard). The tile should compute from those same numeric totals.

findings.title: Zero-budget categories print 'Infinity% over'; a 0-budget or unreadable row turns every bar coordinate into NaN, so the budget chart draws no bars
findings.location: exceptions.js:88 (pct = variance / budget), exceptions.js:150-152, app.js:181 (lim = Math.max(0.3, ...|pct|)), app.js:182,191-193
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/healthbudget.repro.mjs, cases BU-01/AB-01 (committed data + '2026-09,Hay,0,500') and BU-02/AB-02 (committed data + '2026-09,Hay,0,0').
findings.expected: Hay reported in dollars ('$500 spent with no budget'), never 'Infinity%'. A 0/0 placeholder gives no alert and pct 0 or null. The six real categories keep finite bars (Repairs +25%, Fuel +21%, and so on).
findings.actual: BU-01: "serious | Hay | Infinity% over season to date ($500)". AB-01: chart bars "NaN/NaN" ×7, 36 attributes with NaN/Infinity, labels include "+Infinity%", console "Error: <line> attribute x1: Expected length, \"NaN\".". BU-02: "pct=NaN; (no alerts)". AB-02: chart bars "NaN/NaN" ×7, 21 NaN attributes, label "−NaN%".
findings.consequence: A new unbudgeted line (hay bought in a dry year) or an empty placeholder category blanks the entire spending chart. The alert reads 'Infinity% over', which looks broken to a reviewer and gives the manager no sense of the dollars involved.
findings.regression_test: budgetStatus([{category:'Hay',budget:0,actual:0}])[0].pct must not be NaN (expect 0 or null). findExceptions with Hay 0/500 -> exactly one Hay row whose problem contains '$500' and does not match /Infinity|NaN/. Browser: committed data + Hay 0/500 -> #budgetChart has 0 attributes matching /NaN|Infinity/, and the 'Repairs' label is still '+25%' (9,000/7,200 − 1).
findings.proposed_fix: In budgetStatus set pct = budget > 0 ? variance / budget : null and add an unbudgeted = budget === 0 && actual > 0 flag. In findExceptions, add a separate rule for unbudgeted spend with the dollar amount ('$500 spent with no budget line'). In budget(), compute lim only over finite pct values and draw null-pct rows as a labelled 'no budget' marker; label them 'n/a', not ±NaN%.

findings.title: An open health task with a blank or unreadable next_due is never shown anywhere
findings.location: exceptions.js:141 (`|| !h.next_due` → continue), exceptions.js:142-146 (a NaN `left` falls through both branches)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/healthbudget.repro.mjs, cases H-03 ('Heifers,Pregnancy check,2026-09-20,,open') and H-04 (next_due 'TBD').
findings.expected: A warning row for 'Heifers: Pregnancy check', such as 'Open task with no due date' or 'due date "TBD" can't be read', with the action 'Set a due date'.
findings.consequence: Misleading all-clear. An open pregnancy check or vaccination that nobody has scheduled is exactly what a manager needs to see. The page has no health table, so the task is invisible.
findings.regression_test: findExceptions with only the health row 'Heifers,Pregnancy check,2026-09-20,,open' (as_of 2026-09-30T18:00) -> exactly one Health alert, severity 'warning', subject 'Heifers: Pregnancy check', problem matching /no due date/i. The same for next_due 'TBD' with problem matching /TBD|can't be read/i.
findings.proposed_fix: For open tasks, if next_due is blank or Date.parse(next_due) is NaN, push ex('warning','Health', subject, next_due ? `Due date "${next_due}" can't be read` : 'Open, with no due date recorded', 'Set a due date'). Add this row to the rules table and the README.

findings.title: Committed 'Fly tag check' row (status done, last_done Jun 5, next_due Sep 1) contradicts itself and is never flagged; last_done is never read
findings.expected: A row for 'Cows: Fly tag check'. Either 'Overdue by 29 days (due 2026-09-01)' (Sep 1 -> Sep 30 = 29 days), if next_due is the next recurrence, or 'Marked done but next due date passed (last done 2026-06-05)'.
findings.actual: H-05 health alerts: "serious | Yearlings: Booster vaccine | Overdue by 15 days ... || warning | Cows: Pinkeye check | Due in 3 days ...". There is no Fly tag row.
findings.consequence: Under the natural reading (the June check was done, the next one fell due Sep 1, and nothing records it since), a recurring task is 29 days overdue and the dashboard says nothing. A ranch-manager reviewer reading health.csv can spot this in the portfolio's own sample data. The data model doesn't say whether next_due on a 'done' row still matters.
findings.regression_test: After choosing semantics: an inline row 'Cows,Fly tag check,2026-06-05,2026-09-01,done' with as_of 2026-09-30 -> one Health row for 'Cows: Fly tag check'. Its problem is either 'Overdue by 29 days (due 2026-09-01)' (30 − 1 = 29, counted on the calendar) or matches /done.*next due.*passed/i. Then either update the generator row so the fictional data is consistent (e.g. last_done 2026-09-01, next_due blank) and keep EXC.length at 10, or keep the row as a planted problem and raise the count to 11 in the README and test.
findings.proposed_fix: Document what next_due means. If next_due means the next recurrence, judge every row that isn't cancelled by next_due, and use last_done >= next_due to mean the current cycle is done. Otherwise add a consistency check: status done with last_done < next_due <= as_of -> warning 'Record conflict'. Fix the generator row and the README to match.

findings.title: Budget severity is percent only: $30 over on $200 is serious, $9,500 over on $100,000 is a warning, $4,000 is ignored
findings.expected: The $9,500 overrun ranked at least as high as the $30 one. A $4,000 overrun shown at least as a note.
findings.actual: "serious | Ear tags | 15% over season to date ($30) | Find what drove it and decide whether to re-forecast  ||  warning | Feed | 10% over season to date | Watch it next month". Hay ($4,000, 4%) has no row.
findings.consequence: False alarm on small categories ('find what drove it' for $30) and under-ranking of the overruns that actually hurt cash flow. A feed overrun of $9,500 gets 'watch it next month'.
findings.regression_test: With the proposed RULES.budgetMinDollars = 500 and RULES.budgetSeriousDollars = 5000: Ear tags 230/200 -> no row ($30 < $500). Feed 109,500/100,000 -> serious ($9,500 ≥ $5,000). Hay 104,000/100,000 -> warning (4% but $4,000 ≥ $500, if a dollar-only warning is adopted). Expected dollar amounts are by subtraction: 230−200, 109,500−100,000, 104,000−100,000.
findings.proposed_fix: Add dollar thresholds to RULES. Require variance >= budgetMinDollars for any row. Make a row serious when pct > budgetSerious and variance >= a floor, or when variance >= budgetSeriousDollars whatever the percent. Show dollars in every budget row and sort budget rows by dollars.

findings.title: Ties within a severity are sorted A-Z by area, so Budget overruns head the serious block, above an overdue vaccination and a silent water sensor
findings.expected: Under the stated 'worst first' design, the Water (T6 not reporting, near Cedar Draw) and Health (booster 15 days overdue) serious rows come before the Fuel/Repairs overruns.
findings.actual: "1. Budget: Fuel | 2. Budget: Repairs | 3. Gain: Heifers | 4. Grazing: Yearlings in Sand Hills | 5. Health: Yearlings: Booster vaccine | 6. Water: Tank T6 (Cedar Draw)"
findings.consequence: Rows ordered by spelling. A crew lead reading top-down sees the fuel bill before a water tank nobody can see and an overdue vaccination, both of which are time-critical for animal welfare. Budget overruns are month-end decisions but share the 'serious' tier with same-day field problems.
findings.regression_test: On the committed data, the serious rows' areas in order must be ['Water','Health','Grazing','Gain','Budget','Budget'], or at least the indexes of the Water and Health rows must be lower than the index of the first Budget row. The order is set by the proposed priority list, not by the sort code.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the alphabetical tie-break with an explicit AREA_PRIORITY (Water, Health, Grazing, Gain, Budget). Optionally cap budget at 'warning' unless the dollar threshold is met. Describe the ordering in the README.

findings.title: Budget boundaries: exactly 5.0% gets no row though the rules say '5-10%'; 9.6% and 10.4% both print '10% over' at different severities
findings.expected: 5.0% -> warning, as the rules text '5-10%' reads. Two different severities should never show the same percentage. Expected text: 9.6% warning, 10.4% serious.
findings.actual: BU-08: "(no alerts)". BU-09: "9.6%: warning | X | 10% over season to date | Watch it next month  ##  10.4%: serious | X | 10% over season to date ($104) | Find what drove it ...". HB-C7 (exactly 10.0%): "warning | X | 10% over season to date".
findings.consequence: Two rows that both read '10% over' get different severities and actions, which undermines trust in the thresholds. A category exactly 5% over contradicts the published rule text.
findings.regression_test: 1,050 vs 1,000 -> warning '5.0% over season to date' (50/1,000). 1,096 vs 1,000 -> warning '9.6% over' (96/1,000). 1,104 vs 1,000 -> serious '10.4% over' (104/1,000). 1,100 vs 1,000 -> warning '10.0% over' (exactly 10% is not 'more than 10%').
findings.proposed_fix: Pick inclusive bounds and state them exactly: warning at 5% or more up to 10%, serious above 10%. Use >= for the warning bound. Print the percentage to one decimal ((pct*100).toFixed(1)). Fix the rules-table and README text to match.

findings.title: With amounts in cents, a floating-point sum tips an exact 10.00% overrun into 'serious' (pct 0.10000000000000007)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/healthbudget.repro.mjs, case BU-10. Budgets 1265.97, 1631.6, 1855.07, 2666.36; actuals 2041.13, 2043.68, 2039.34, 2036.75 (one row per month, Jun-Sep, category X).
findings.expected: Warning, the same as the whole-dollar 1,100 vs 1,000 case. In integer cents: budget 741,900c, actual 816,090c, over 74,190c, exactly 10%.
findings.actual: "integer-cent check: budget 741900c actual 816090c exactly 10% = true; code budget=7419 actual=8160.900000000001 pct=0.10000000000000007; serious | X | 10% over season to date ($741.9)"
findings.consequence: Exactly at the threshold, severity depends on how the cents happen to round in binary floating point. This is rare, but real ledgers carry cents. With whole dollars it does not happen (HB-C7 gives pct exactly 0.1).
findings.regression_test: Feed the four rows above through findExceptions. Expect a warning row for X. The expected value comes from integer-cent arithmetic (74,190 × 10 = 741,900), not from the float formula.
findings.proposed_fix: Sum in integer cents (Math.round(x*100)) and compare variance_cents*100 against budget_cents*threshold_pct_int, or round pct to 6 decimal places before comparing.

findings.title: Budget alert dollars are raw toLocaleString ('$104.5', '$741.9') and warning rows carry no dollars at all
findings.expected: '$105' (the table's whole-dollar style, '+$105') or '$104.50'. The warning row should also include '$60'.
findings.actual: "serious | X | 10% over season to date ($104.5) ...  ##  warning: warning | X | 6% over season to date | Watch it next month"
findings.consequence: Cosmetic, but money shown as '$104.5' looks unpolished in a portfolio piece. A warning row gives the manager no dollar figure to judge it by.
findings.regression_test: 1,104.50 vs 1,000 -> the problem contains '($105)'. 104.5 rounds half up to 105, the same as money() in the table. 1,060 vs 1,000 -> the warning problem contains '$60'.
findings.proposed_fix: Move money() from app.js into exceptions.js, export it, and use it in both rule texts (and in the table). Add the dollar figure to the warning text.

findings.title: Spend vs budget tile shows '−0.0%' when exactly on budget and '−NaN% $0 of $0' with no budget rows; on-budget bars read '−0%' and 'Under by $0'
findings.location: app.js:57 (sign from ta > tb; divides by tb), app.js:193 (label sign), app.js:194 (tooltip Over/Under)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/healthbudget.repro.mjs, cases AB-04 (every actual set equal to its budget) and AB-05 (budget.csv with only its header).
findings.expected: AB-04: tile '0.0%' with no minus, or 'On budget', and '$88,400 of $88,400'. Bar labels '0%'. Tooltip 'On budget'. AB-05: a 'No budget loaded' text with no NaN.
findings.actual: AB-04 tile: "SPEND VS BUDGET −0.0% $88,400 of $88,400, season to date". Labels: "−0%" for all six. Tooltip: "Water and fencing Budget $4,800 Actual $4,800 Under by $0". AB-05 tile: "SPEND VS BUDGET −NaN% $0 of $0, season to date".
findings.consequence: Cosmetic and misleading in edge cases: on budget is shown as 'under', and an empty budget file prints NaN in the headline tile.
findings.regression_test: Browser with every actual = budget -> the tile matches /SPEND VS BUDGET 0\.0%/ and contains '$88,400 of $88,400'. 88,400 is the sum of the committed monthly budgets ×4. No chart label matches /−0%/. Header-only budget.csv -> the tile does not match /NaN/.
findings.proposed_fix: Compute d = (ta − tb) / tb only when tb > 0, otherwise show 'No budget loaded'. Take the sign from the rounded value (+ if > 0, none if 0, − if < 0). Use the same rule for bar labels. When variance === 0 the tooltip says 'On budget'.

findings.title: 'Due in 0 days' for a task due today
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/healthbudget.repro.mjs, case H-07 ('Cows,Pinkeye check,2026-08-01,2026-09-30,open', as_of 2026-09-30T18:00). Also reported as TIME-18 in time.repro.mjs.
findings.expected: 'Due today (2026-09-30)', with an action that fits a same-day task.
findings.actual: "warning | Cows: Pinkeye check | Due in 0 days (2026-09-30) | Plan it with the next gather"
findings.consequence: Awkward wording, and the action 'Plan it with the next gather' for something due today means it goes overdue tomorrow unless someone acts.
findings.regression_test: The inline row above -> problem === 'Due today (2026-09-30)'. A row due Oct 1 still reads 'Due in 1 day (2026-10-01)'.
findings.proposed_fix: if (left === 0) use 'Due today (D)' with the action 'Do it today or set a new date'. Keep the existing branches for 1..7.

findings.title: next_due with a time part ('2026-09-30 00:00:00') gives fractional days and flips severity with the viewer's time zone
findings.location: exceptions.js:36 (days via new Date on both strings), exceptions.js:142-146
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/healthbudget.repro.mjs, case H-08 (row 'Cows,Pinkeye check,2026-08-01,2026-09-30 00:00:00,open', run with TZ America/Chicago and Europe/Berlin).
findings.expected: The same whole-day result in every zone: due today, warning.
findings.actual: "Chicago: warning | Cows: Pinkeye check | Due in 0.20833333333333334 days (2026-09-30 00:00:00) ...  ##  Berlin: serious | Cows: Pinkeye check | Overdue by 0.08333333333333333 days (due 2026-09-30 00:00:00) | Schedule it this week"
findings.consequence: A common database or Excel export format puts 16-digit decimals on screen, and the same task is 'serious, overdue' for one viewer and 'warning' for another. Low, because the documented format is date-only; the related date-format cases are covered by the time auditor.
findings.regression_test: Run under TZ=America/Chicago and TZ=Europe/Berlin. Both give exactly one warning with the problem 'Due today (2026-09-30)' (or 'Due in 0 days' before the wording fix). Nothing matches /\d\.\d/.
findings.proposed_fix: Normalise next_due to its first 10 characters after checking it with /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}/. Otherwise report the date as unreadable (see the no-due-date finding). Compute days with Date.UTC parts and Math.round.

findings.title: Open task whose last_done is after next_due is reported 'Overdue ... Schedule it this week' (risk of a repeat treatment)
findings.expected: A 'record conflict' row: done 2026-09-20 after due 2026-09-15 but still open; confirm and close it, or set the next date.
findings.actual: "serious | Yearlings: Booster vaccine | Overdue by 15 days (due 2026-09-15) | Schedule it this week"
findings.consequence: If the crew gave the booster on Sep 20 and nobody updated the status, the report tells them to schedule it again: wasted vaccine and labour, and a possible double dose.
findings.regression_test: The inline row above (as_of 2026-09-30) -> one Health warning whose problem matches /last done 2026-09-20.*after.*due 2026-09-15/i and whose action is not 'Schedule it this week'.
findings.proposed_fix: When status is open and last_done >= next_due, emit a warning 'Done <last_done> after due <next_due> but still open: confirm the record' with the action 'Confirm with the crew before scheduling'.

findings.title: Budget chart: a category about 25% or more under budget draws its value label on top of its category name
findings.location: app.js:180-193 (m.l = 140; value label at a − 6, text-anchor end; category label at m.l − 10)
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/healthbudget.repro.mjs, case AB-09 (committed data with every 'Water and fencing' actual set to 720, i.e. 60% of 1,200).
findings.expected: The '−40%' label does not overlap the 'Water and fencing' label (2,880/4,800 − 1 = −40%).
findings.actual: "chart labels=[... \"Water and fencing\",\"−40%\"]", bar "140/183" (it starts at the left edge), "'Water and fencing' label overlaps its value label: true".
findings.consequence: The most under-budget category, usually the one worth asking about (for example, skipped fence or vet work), becomes unreadable.
findings.regression_test: In the browser with that data, getBBox() of the 'Water and fencing' label and of its value label do not intersect horizontally.
findings.proposed_fix: Leave room for labels on the left (x range from m.l + 40), or draw negative-value labels inside the bar or to the right of zero.

findings.title: Rules table prints floating-point noise when a budget threshold is tuned (0.07 -> '7.000000000000001-10%')
findings.repro: node docs/audit/diagnostics/healthbudget.repro.mjs, case AB-06 (exceptions.js served with budgetWarn: 0.07).
findings.actual: "Budget Warning A category is 7.000000000000001-10% over budget"
findings.consequence: The README invites ranches to tune RULES, and the first tweak puts visible float noise on the page.
findings.regression_test: In the browser with budgetWarn 0.07, the Budget warning rules row contains '7-10% over budget'. 7 is 0.07 as a percentage, checked by hand.
findings.proposed_fix: Format with a helper: const pct = (v) => +(v * 100).toFixed(2) + '%'. Use it for every RULES-derived percentage in rules(); the gain rows have the same pattern.

checked_ok: Committed health.csv gives exactly two health alerts, matching hand counts (HB-C1): "serious | Yearlings: Booster vaccine | Overdue by 15 days (due 2026-09-15) | Schedule it this week  ||  warning | Cows: Pinkeye check | Due in 3 days (2026-10-03) | Plan it with the next gather". Pregnancy check (25 days out) and Deworm (32 days out) correctly have no row.

Committed budget.csv gives exactly Fuel and Repairs, matching hand sums (HB-C2): "serious | Fuel | 21% over season to date ($2,040) ... || serious | Repairs | 25% over season to date ($1,800)". Fuel: 11,640 vs 9,600. Repairs: 9,000 vs 7,200.

Committed tile, chart and table are right (AB-00): tile "SPEND VS BUDGET +1.0% $89,303 of $88,400, season to date"; labels "Repairs +25%, Fuel +21%, Vet and health −1%, Feed and mineral −3%, Labor −5%, Water and fencing −7%" in descending order; 0 NaN attributes; table "Feed and mineral $24,800 $24,002 −$798", "Fuel $9,600 $11,640 +$2,040". Negative variances show as −$ and positives as +$.

Health singular/plural wording and the 7-day edge (HB-C3): "Overdue by 1 day (due 2026-09-29)", "Due in 1 day (2026-10-01)", "Due in 7 days (2026-10-07)", and nothing for Oct 8. This matches the README's 'within 7 days' (inclusive).

Health day counts are the same in every viewer zone for date-only values (HB-C8): identical text in UTC, America/Chicago and Australia/Sydney. A separate shell loop over UTC, Chicago, Denver, Sydney and Kiritimati gave identical Health and Budget alerts.
A health task for a group not in groups.csv is still reported (HB-C4): "serious | Bulls: Trich test | Overdue by 10 days (due 2026-09-20)".
Status 'cancelled' and 'done' (one-off tasks) are not flagged (HB-C5): "(no alerts)".
Credits written with a minus sign sum correctly (HB-C6): "actual=5820 variance=-1380 pct=-0.19166666666666668; (no alerts)" (1620+2520+1980−300 = 5,820).

The suspected float problem at the 10% boundary does not happen with whole dollars (HB-C7): 1,100 vs 1,000 gives "pct=0.1; warning | X | 10% over season to date". The code computes (a−b)/b = 100/1000, a correctly rounded division that equals the literal 0.1, not 1100/1000−1 (which would be 0.10000000000000009). Exactly 10% is a warning, which matches 'more than 10%' for serious. The float drift only appears when amounts carry cents (BU-10).
On the committed data the budget table and chart agree in sign and magnitude with the alert rows. No page errors or console errors in the control run (AB-00: "page errors=[]; console errors=0").
Rules-table text for the default thresholds is clean: 0.1*100 = 10 and 0.05*100 = 5 exactly (node printed "10 5"). The float noise only appears for values like 0.07 (AB-06).
